passage:
autonomy — 自主权；自治
Some companies have responded by creating “autonomy audits.” In these audits, managers and employees review together how much choice workers actually have in their daily tasks.

discretion — 自行决定的自由；酌情权
In her view, employees often accept these tools because they promise efficiency, but they may not realize how much discretion they are giving up.

algorithm — 算法
Warehouse staff said that their break times were now set by an algorithm rather than by their team leader.

predictability — 可预测性
A survey of 400 employees in the logistics sector found that most respondents valued the predictability of automated schedules.

monitored — 被监控的
However, a significant minority—about one in five—reported feeling monitored and stressed.

skeptical — 怀疑的
Critics, however, remain skeptical.

undermine — 削弱；暗中破坏
She points out that some managers welcome the data these systems provide, while others worry that the tools undermine their own judgment.

neutral — 中立的；不偏不倚的
Lena Ortiz, a workplace researcher, argues that such changes are rarely neutral.
